# Standards and Taxonomy Crosswalk

This is the human-readable view of [`STANDARDS-CROSSWALK.json`](STANDARDS-CROSSWALK.json). It compares concepts, not legal obligations. “Correspondence” means that CAM contains a relevant concept; it does not mean equivalence, adoption, conformance or compliant deployment.

| External comparison area | CAM determination | Status | Next repair path |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ISO/NIST organisational governance and lifecycle risk | Instruments, ledgers and repair logic exist, but CAM is not an organisational AI management system. | partial-crosswalk | Optional implementation-assurance profile after authorised source review. |
| SPDX/CycloneDX AI-BOM | AI-ABOM is broader than a component list and supports incident-time state; no exchange schema or validation exists. | strong-conceptual-correspondence | Design a compositional implementation profile, not a competing BOM. |
| Singapore agentic governance | CAM’s authority, execution, escalation, handoff and arbitration separations are strong; deployer checklist coverage is incomplete. | strong-conceptual-correspondence | Apply as a practical review lens while preserving separate CAM authority axes. |
| Embodied lifecycle identity | CAM carefully distinguishes substrate, registry and continuity, but STEWARD-005 is Draft. | present-but-not-crosswalked | Adoption/locality review, then neutral record profile. |
| Entity/system/model/component taxonomy | Useful distinctions exist; no reviewable entity threshold separates scientific classification from identity or moral-status claims. | gap | Dedicated entity-threshold research before taxonomy drafting. |
| Relational cardinality | Mechanisms are meaningful, but dyadic/triadic/polyadic are not controlled terms in the reviewed external sources. | intentional-divergence | Contextual migration to two-party, three-party and multi-party/multi-actor language. |
| Registry versus personhood | CAM’s separation of registration, continuity, identity and rights is an important safeguard. | strong-conceptual-correspondence | Retain the non-inference boundary. |
